title: Present Perfect Continuous: Process, Duration & Visible Effects
grammarTitle: Present Perfect Continuous — Process, Duration & Choosing Between PPS and PPC
grammarNote: Present Perfect Continuous (have/has been + -ing) акцентирует ПРОЦЕСС и ПРОДОЛЖИТЕЛЬНОСТЬ, а не результат. Выбор между PPS и PPC — один из самых тонких аспектов английской грамматики на уровне B1-B2. Правило не всегда однозначное, но понимание разницы в акцентах делает вашу речь значительно точнее.

grammarTable.subject: Duration up to now
grammarTable.example: "I've been waiting for 2 hours." / "We've been living here since 2020." ✅

grammarTable.subject: Ongoing process
grammarTable.example: "She's been working on the thesis all day." / "He's been trying to call." ✅

grammarTable.subject: Explains present state
grammarTable.example: "You're out of breath — have you been running?" ✅

grammarTable.subject: Temporary ongoing activity
grammarTable.example: "I've been reading this book for a week." (still reading) ✅

grammarTable.subject: PPS vs PPC: result vs process
grammarTable.example: "She's written three chapters." (PPS: 3 done) vs "She's been writing all day." (PPC: process ongoing) ✅

grammarTable.subject: Counting → PPS only
grammarTable.example: ✗ "She's been writing 3 papers." → ✅ "She's WRITTEN 3 papers." — count = PPS ✅

grammarExtra.title: When PPC is more natural than PPS

rows.example: "I've been studying FOR three hours." (process matters, not the result) ✅
"She's sweating. She must have been running." (running explains the sweat) ✅
"I've been working on this code all day. I'm not finished yet." ✅
"You've been crying." (eyes are still red — the crying just stopped) ✅
"I've been trying to contact you for hours!" (emphasis on the effort) ✅

grammarExtra.title: When PPS is more natural than PPC

rows.example: "She has WRITTEN three papers this year." ✅ NOT "has been writing three papers" ✗
"I've FINISHED the report." (done — result exists) ✅
"I've KNOWN him for years." ✅ NEVER "been knowing" ✗
"Have you BEEN to Almaty?" (experience) ✅
"She's CALLED three times." (each call = a completion) ✅

grammarExtra.title: Cases where BOTH are natural — different emphasis

rows.example: "I've worked here" = credential/achievement. Three years is a completed stretch. ✅
"I've been working" = the work is ongoing. Still here, still in it. ✅
"She's read the book" = completed; result (she knows what's in it). ✅
"She's been reading" = still in progress; or explains a visible state. ✅
Ask: Is the RESULT or the PROCESS the focus? Result = PPS. Process = PPC. ✅

grammarExtra.title: PPC with stative verbs — grey areas

rows.example: "I've lived here for 3 years." ✅ AND "I've been living here for 3 years." ✅
"She's worked here for 5 years." ✅ AND "She's been working here for 5 years." ✅
"I've stayed here before." ✅ (experience) / "I've been staying here for a week." ✅ (process)
"Lived" (PPS) = settled, completed stretch. "Been living" (PPC) = ongoing, still in it. ✅
✅ "I've WRITTEN 3 papers." — counting = PPS. ✅
✅ "I've KNOWN her for years." — stative = PPS. ✅
✅ "I've FINISHED the report." — completed result = PPS. ✅
✅ "She's been READING the book." OR "She's READ the book." — check: are you using -ing? ✅

grammarTip:
Present Perfect Continuous:
have/has + been + V-ing

USE PPC for:
→ DURATION (how long something has been happening)
  "I've been waiting FOR two hours."
  "She's been studying SINCE this morning."

→ ONGOING PROCESS (still in progress)
  "He's been writing all day — not finished yet."

→ EXPLAINING VISIBLE STATE
  "You look tired — have you been running?"

CHOOSE PPS INSTEAD when:
→ Counting: "She's WRITTEN 3 papers." ✅
→ Result matters: "I've FINISHED." ✅
→ Stative verb: "I've KNOWN her." ✅

BOTH possible (different emphasis):
"I've worked here for 3 years." (achievement)
"I've been working here for 3 years." (ongoing)

Key question: RESULT or PROCESS?
→ Result focus = PPS
→ Process focus = PPC

exercises.text: "She ___ (study) for the exam all day. She looks exhausted."
exercises.hint: Duration + explains present state (exhausted) = PPC. "She HAS BEEN STUDYING all day." ✅

exercises.text: "Why are his clothes covered in oil? He ___ (fix) his bike."
exercises.hint: Explains visible state (oil-covered clothes) = PPC. "He HAS BEEN FIXING his bike." ✅

exercises.instruction: PPS or PPC? Count vs duration.
exercises.hint: Counting = PPS. "She HAS WRITTEN 5 emails." ✅ NOT "has been writing 5 emails" ✗

exercises.text: "I ___ (work) on this project for three weeks. I'm still not done."
opts: Both are correct — process ongoing, PPC preferred
exercises.correct: Both are correct — process ongoing, PPC preferred
exercises.hint: "I've been working on this project for three weeks" (PPC — process/duration) ✅ / "I've worked" also possible. PPC is preferred when emphasising "still not done." ✅

exercises.text: "I can't talk now. I ___ (try) to finish this report."
exercises.hint: "I'VE BEEN TRYING to finish this report." — ongoing effort, explaining current state. ✅
Completed result (here it is) = PPS. "I HAVE FINISHED the report." ✅
"Have you BEEN CRYING?" — PPC explains visible state (red eyes). ✅

exercises.text: "The phone has ___ (ring) all morning. Nobody answers."
opts: Both been ringing and rung work
exercises.correct: Both been ringing and rung work
exercises.hint: "has BEEN RINGING" (PPC — ongoing process) ✅ / "has RUNG" (PPS — also natural). Both possible. ✅

opts: "been knowing" is wrong — "know" is stative; should be "known"
exercises.correct: "been knowing" is wrong — "know" is stative; should be "known"
exercises.hint: ✅ "She's KNOWN him since university." — stative verb "know" → PPS only. ✅

exercises.instruction: Same event, different focus. Choose PPS.
exercises.text: Focus on the result: she has completed this. "She ___ (write) the introduction."
exercises.hint: "She HAS WRITTEN the introduction." (PPS = completed, result). "Has been writing" = still in process. ✅

exercises.text: "I ___ in Almaty for three years now." — Which is correct?
opts: Both are natural — "live" works with both forms
exercises.correct: Both are natural — "live" works with both forms
exercises.hint: "I've LIVED in Almaty for 3 years." ✅ AND "I've BEEN LIVING in Almaty for 3 years." ✅ — both natural with "live." ✅

exercises.text: "You smell like coffee! ___ (you / drink) coffee all morning?"
exercises.hint: "HAVE YOU BEEN DRINKING coffee all morning?" — PPC explains the smell (visible state). ✅

exercises.text: "The team ___ the report since Monday." (still writing, focus on duration)
exercises.hint: "Has BEEN WRITING since Monday" (PPC) = still in process, duration is the focus. ✅

exercises.text: "He ___ four books this year." vs "He ___ a lot this year."
exercises.hint: "HAS WRITTEN four books" (PPS — counting) ✅ + "HAS BEEN READING a lot" (PPC — process/duration). ✅

exercises.text: "I ___ (try) to fix this bug for three days now. It's driving me mad."
opts: Both have tried and have been trying work
exercises.correct: Both have tried and have been trying work
exercises.hint: "I'VE TRIED to fix this bug for three days." (PPS — number of attempts) ✅ / "I'VE BEEN TRYING" (PPC — ongoing frustrating effort) ✅ — both work, different nuance. ✅

exercises.text: "She's been analysing the data since Wednesday." — What does this emphasise?
opts: The number of data points analysed
The duration and ongoing process of the analysis
exercises.correct: The duration and ongoing process of the analysis
exercises.hint: PPC = emphasises duration ("since Wednesday") and that the analysis is still ongoing. ✅

opts: Duration and ongoing processes up to now
questions.correct: Duration and ongoing processes up to now
questions.hint: PPC = how long something has been happening; process still in progress. ✅

questions.text: "I've been waiting for two hours." — "have been waiting" because:
opts: The waiting is the ongoing process; duration is the focus
questions.correct: The waiting is the ongoing process; duration is the focus
questions.hint: PPC for duration of ongoing activity. "FOR two hours." ✅

questions.text: "She's been writing 3 essays." — What is wrong?
opts: "3 essays" = counting → should be PPS: "She's written 3 essays"
questions.correct: "3 essays" = counting → should be PPS: "She's written 3 essays"
questions.hint: ✅ Counting = PPS. "She's WRITTEN 3 essays." PPC cannot count. ✅

questions.text: "You look tired — have you been running?" — PPC because:
opts: PPC explains the visible present state through recent ongoing activity
questions.correct: PPC explains the visible present state through recent ongoing activity
questions.hint: PPC = explains why someone looks a certain way. The running → explains the tiredness. ✅

questions.text: "She ___ (work) on her thesis ALL semester. It's almost done."
questions.hint: "She HAS BEEN WORKING on her thesis all semester." — ongoing duration, process. ✅

questions.text: "I've been knowing him for years." — Error:
questions.hint: "know" = stative → PPS only. "I'VE KNOWN him for years." ✅

opts: "She's been writing the report all day."
questions.correct: "She's been writing the report all day."
questions.hint: "She's been WRITING the report all day." = PPC correct form. ✅ All others have errors.

questions.text: PPS vs PPC: "She's written 3 chapters." vs "She's been writing all day." — difference:
opts: "Written 3 chapters" = result/count; "been writing all day" = process/duration
questions.correct: "Written 3 chapters" = result/count; "been writing all day" = process/duration
questions.hint: PPS = result (3 chapters done). PPC = process (all day long). ✅

questions.text: "I've been working here for 3 years." vs "I've worked here for 3 years." — which is true?
opts: Both are correct — "been working" = still ongoing; "worked" = also natural
questions.correct: Both are correct — "been working" = still ongoing; "worked" = also natural
questions.hint: "live/work/stay" = grey area verbs that work with both PPS and PPC for duration. ✅

questions.text: When should you definitely choose PPC over PPS?
opts: When emphasising the duration or ongoing process of a dynamic verb
questions.correct: When emphasising the duration or ongoing process of a dynamic verb
questions.hint: PPC = when the process/duration matters. "I've BEEN STUDYING for 3 hours." ✅
"How long HAS SHE BEEN STUDYING?" — duration → PPC. ✅

questions.text: "It has been raining since this morning." — PPC correct because:
opts: Rain is ongoing from this morning to now; duration + process
questions.correct: Rain is ongoing from this morning to now; duration + process
questions.hint: PPC + since = activity ongoing from starting point to now. "BEEN RAINING since this morning." ✅
